transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Um… I’m a little embarrassed to say it, because I know it might sound strange. But what scared me enough to come in is… I’ve been hearing my name called when nobody’s there. Like from the hallway at home, and once at the warehouse too.

It sounds real—like as real as my husband standing right next to me. I wasn’t sure if I should even mention it, but… that’s the part that’s been worrying me.
Have you noticed any other sounds, voices, or things that others around you don’t seem to hear or notice?

Mostly just that… my name being called. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it really does sound like someone is there—like in the hallway at home, and that one time at the warehouse. Then I check, and nobody’s there.

I haven’t really noticed other sounds, not that I can think of. It’s just… that one is what scared me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you noticed any other types of sounds, voices, or experiences that other people around you don’t seem to notice—like seeing things, feeling something on your skin, or maybe smelling something unusual?

No, not really seeing things or feeling things on my skin… and I haven’t noticed smells like that. It’s mostly just the voice—or sound, I guess—calling my name.

It happens like from the hallway at home, and once at the warehouse, and it sounds completely real. Like… as real as if my husband was standing right there saying it. Then I look, and no one’s there. I’m sorry, I know that probably sounds odd, but that’s the main thing I’ve noticed.
Have you had any thoughts or beliefs that others might not share—like ideas that you know are unusual but feel very real to you?

I mean… I don’t think I believed anything too out there, exactly. But I guess there was this thing where I got really sure that I could take my crafts and turn them into a real retirement business right away.

At the time it felt like… not just an idea, but like I’d figured out the perfect plan for our family, and once people saw it they’d understand I was right. Saying it now, I know maybe that sounds a little big. I don’t want to make it sound like I thought I was special or anything, but it felt very real to me then.
Have you ever had a belief that something was definitely true, even when others told you it wasn’t, and you felt certain despite what they said?

I guess… yes, kind of. Not anything strange-strange, I don’t think, but with the crafts I really got it in my head that I could turn it into a retirement business right away. Like I had figured out this perfect plan for us, for my family, and everyone would see it once I explained it.

My husband didn’t really see it that way, and I think other people were trying to be realistic, but at the time I felt so sure they just weren’t understanding yet. Saying it out loud now, I can hear how big that sounds… but back then it felt completely true.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that others might not share or that seem unusual, but felt completely true to you at the time?

I don’t think there was anything else like… bizarre, if that’s what you mean. The main thing was still that craft business idea.

I really did get it in my head that I could make it into a real retirement business right away, like I had somehow figured out the perfect plan for our family. And I felt like once everybody heard me out, they’d see it too. I know now that might have been… a lot, maybe unrealistic. But at the time it felt completely true to me.
Have you ever had any other beliefs or ideas that felt completely true to you at the time, even if others didn’t see things the same way or tried to tell you otherwise?

I think it’s mostly that same thing, honestly. I don’t want to overstate it, because I didn’t think I was, you know, better than everyone or anything. But I did get really convinced that my crafts could become this real retirement business right away.

At the time it felt like I’d figured out the perfect plan for my family, and if people just listened, they’d see it too. My husband didn’t really agree, but I thought he just wasn’t seeing the whole picture yet. Looking back, I can see maybe I was more sure than I should’ve been. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs or ideas that felt completely true to you, even when others tried to tell you they weren’t real or didn’t make sense?

I think… no, not really anything separate from what I already mentioned. It was mainly that crafts idea.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but I really did believe I could turn it into a real retirement business right away, like I’d figured out the perfect plan for our family. And when people didn’t agree, I felt like they just weren’t seeing it yet. Looking back, I can see why that might not have made sense to everyone… but at the time it felt very true to me.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that felt completely true to you, even when others told you they weren’t real or tried to convince you otherwise?

I think it’s still mostly that same crafts thing. I’m sorry if I’m repeating myself.

At the time, I really got it in my head that I could turn my crafts into a real retirement business right away, and that I’d figured out this perfect plan for my family. Like if everyone would just hear me out, they’d understand I was right. Looking back, I can see maybe I was too sure of it… but then it felt completely true to me.

Have you ever had any other times where you believed something very strongly that others didn’t share or tried to tell you wasn’t true—something that felt completely real to you, even if it might not have made sense to them?

I don’t think there was another big belief, no… I mean, not apart from that crafts idea I keep coming back to.

I know it probably sounds a little unrealistic now, but at the time I really felt like I’d figured something out — like I could turn my crafts into a retirement business right away, and that it was the perfect plan for my family. I felt like if everyone could just see it the way I did, they’d understand I was right.

I’m not trying to make excuses. It just felt very real to me then.

Have you ever had a time when you believed something very strongly that wasn’t true, and even when people tried to tell you otherwise, you still felt certain it was real—like something you could feel in your gut was true, even if it didn’t make sense to others?

Yeah… I think the closest thing is still that crafts idea. I don’t want to make it sound like I thought I was some genius or anything, but I really did feel certain, in my gut, that I could turn it into a retirement business right away.

Like, I had this feeling that I’d figured out the perfect plan for our family, and everyone else would eventually see it if they just understood what I was seeing. Even when people questioned it, I didn’t really take that in at the time. I just felt like… no, this is real, this is going to work.

Looking back, I can see why that might’ve seemed like too much. But then, yes, I believed it very strongly.

Have you ever had a strong belief about something that turned out not to be true, but at the time you felt absolutely certain about it—even if it was different from the craft business idea you mentioned?

I’m trying to think if there was something separate from that… and I don’t really want to overstate it.

But honestly, it still comes back to that same feeling I had — that I could make my crafts into a real retirement business right away, and that I’d somehow figured out the perfect plan for my family. At the time I felt so sure, like everyone would see it once I explained it right.

I know now that probably wasn’t realistic the way I was thinking about it, but back then it felt absolutely certain to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you ever had a belief that something in your life was definitely true—like a situation involving people you know, or something happening in a way that others didn’t see—something that felt completely real to you, even though it turned out not to be true?

I think so… I mean, not so much about people doing something to me or anything like that. It was more that I got really fixed on this idea that my crafts could become a real retirement business right away.

At the time it felt completely true, like I had figured out the perfect plan for my family, and if everyone else could just understand it, they’d see it too. I know that probably sounds… overly confident, maybe. But in the moment it didn’t feel questionable to me.

Is that answering what you’re asking?
Have you ever had a belief that someone was acting against you, watching you, or that events in the world were directly related to you in a way others didn’t seem to understand?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt like people weren’t understanding me, or like they were missing what I was trying to explain, but not that they were watching me or acting against me.

And I don’t think I’ve felt like the news or events in the world were about me personally. At least… not that I can remember. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever had a belief that you had special abilities, powers, or a unique role that others didn’t recognize or understand?

Not powers, no… I wouldn’t say it like that. But I guess I did feel like I had this special idea, or like I was seeing something everyone else wasn’t seeing yet.

I got it in my head that I could turn my crafts into a real retirement business right away, and that everybody would eventually realize I’d figured out the perfect plan for our family. At the time it felt… really clear to me, like I just needed people to trust me.

I know now that sounds like I was getting ahead of myself. I’m not trying to make it sound bigger than it was, but maybe that’s close to what you mean?

Have you ever felt that you had special qualities, abilities, or a unique purpose that others didn’t recognize or appreciate — something more than just having a good idea or being particularly skilled at something?

I don’t think it was like a special purpose exactly… at least I don’t want to make it sound that dramatic.

But I did feel like I had figured something out that other people weren’t seeing. I got really sure that I could turn my crafts into a real retirement business right away, and that once everyone understood it, they’d see I had come up with the perfect plan for our family.

At the time it felt more than just being excited about an idea. It felt obvious to me, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you ever felt like certain things in the world, like events on TV, songs playing, or things people say, were sending you special messages or had a hidden meaning meant just for you?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ll hear a song and it might remind me of something, like anybody would, but not like it was meant for me or sending me a message.

And TV or things people say… I don’t think I’ve taken it that way. If I’m understanding you right, no, that hasn’t really happened.

Have you ever felt like certain things in the world, like events happening around you, things people said, or things you saw on TV, were somehow directly related to you or had a special meaning meant just for you?

No… I don’t think so. Not in the way you’re describing.

I can overthink things sometimes, like wonder if someone meant something by a comment, but I don’t remember feeling like TV or events around me were sending me some special meaning just for me. If that’s what you mean, then no, I haven’t really noticed that.

Have you ever had a belief that was completely untrue, but you felt absolutely certain it was real at the time—like something you couldn’t doubt, even when others clearly didn’t share it or tried to tell you it wasn’t true?

I guess… maybe the closest thing was with the crafts idea. I don’t know if I’d call it completely untrue, because it felt like a real possibility to me, but I got very sure that I could turn it into a retirement business right away.

Like, I really believed everyone would eventually see that I had figured out the perfect plan for our family. When people weren’t seeing it that way, I didn’t really take that in at the time. I just felt like they didn’t understand it yet.

I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
